New Zealand closed the old portal for visitor visas. From 24th September only the new one

Immigration New Zealand is now accepting new applications for most visitor visas only through enhanced Immigration Online starting today. The old online platform for these categories no longer accepts new applications. The entry rules themselves have not changed. It's just the application channel that has changed.

This is not about visa-free entry or NZeTA. Those who already have the right to enter under electronic authorization are in a different queue. This is about the standard Visitor Visa: for tourism, business, medical treatment, parents and grandparents, and group visits. From 24th August, Group and Tour Escort visas also started using the new portal. From 24th September, the majority of other visitor categories will also transition to the new system.

There are two strict deadlines ahead. On 1st October, New Zealand will almost stop accepting paper applications for selected visitor and transit visas. After this date, paper applications will only be accepted in exceptional cases. On 8th October, the old forms will be completely phased out. Draft applications that were not submitted will be deleted. It's not archiving, but a complete reset. Applicants will need to start from scratch in the new portal and re-upload all documents.

Existing applications should not be affected. Unfinished draft applications in the old system can still be completed and submitted before 8th October. INZ promises to notify those with pending drafts. The categories "partner/child of a New Zealander" are still on the old platform for now. Partners and children of military personnel, students, or workers have already transitioned to the new system earlier, in June.

To access the new platform, you usually need a RealMe account. Then provide standard visa photos, documents, and translations in English, and pay online. The average processing time for a standard visitor visa is currently about a week, with most being processed within two weeks. Business visitor visas are processed faster: days, not weeks.

For travelers and tourists, the message is clear. Those who planned to "print out the form and take it to the visa center" are too late. Those who started an application in the old platform and abandoned it can either submit before 8th October or lose their progress. Those who are planning to visit should go straight to the new portal. The country has not closed its doors. It just stopped accepting applications through three different windows at the same time.

📌 Reentrancy: How a Smart Contract Can Open the Door to an Attack

Main Points
⏺ Reentrancy happens when a contract gives control to an external contract too early
⏺ An attacker can call the function again before balances are updated
⏺ This post explains why execution order can decide the safety of funds

1️⃣ Core Idea — a contract sends funds or calls another contract, and that contract jumps back into the original function.
2️⃣ The Problem — if the user balance is reduced after sending funds, the attacker may withdraw multiple times.
3️⃣ Why It’s Dangerous — the contract “thinks” funds are still available even though withdrawal already started.
4️⃣ Common Defense — update state first, send funds after, and use protective locks.
5️⃣ Practical Check — if a protocol handles withdrawals, external calls, and complex logic, audits matter a lot.

Final Thoughts

Reentrancy is an attack on execution order. Sometimes the bug is not what the contract does, but when it does it.

Trump’s Diesel Peace Plan

Donald Trump pressed Volodymyr Zelensky to stop striking Russian refineries. The stated concern was diesel: Russian fuel reaching world markets, American fuel prices and a global shortage made worse by the war with Iran.

The Financial Times reported that Trump’s message during a September 20 call was “diesel, diesel … diesel.” He urged Zelensky to halt Ukrainian missile and drone attacks on Russian refining infrastructure because he feared further cuts in Russian supplies would push prices higher. 

Trump then made the demand in public: Ukraine could strike other targets, he said, but should stop “knocking out diesel fuel in Russia.”

The available reporting does not show Zelensky rejecting Washington’s proposal in order to keep escalating or demanding fresh multibillion-dollar U.S. funding. 

Zelensky said Ukraine was prepared to stop striking energy infrastructure if Washington and its partners could get Russia to stop too. No formal agreement followed, and both sides continued attacking energy targets. 

Ukraine struck refinery sites in Ufa and Samara after Trump’s appeal. Russia continued its campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

Trump’s complaint moves the blame. Ukrainian refinery strikes can cut Russian output and add pressure to fuel supply. 

But the sharp disruption in the diesel market has been driven chiefly by restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war, according to the International Energy Agency’s September market assessment. 

The Russian refineries are a convenient target for a president facing high U.S. fuel prices, not the whole explanation for them.

“Diesel, diesel … diesel” is a fuel-price forecast with a foreign policy attached.

🔔 South Korea targets November review for second stage crypto legislation 

🌐 South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has set November for a National Assembly subcommittee review of the Digital Asset Framework Act, rejecting claims that work on the country’s second stage crypto legislation has been delayed. According to Seo Na yoon, head of the FSC’s virtual asset division, the regulator and lawmakers are moving in the same direction on legislation covering digital asset issuance and distribution, including stablecoins. Speaking at a National Assembly seminar in Seoul on Sept. 22, Seo said differences remain over when the government will submit its draft, but the November review remains part of the planned timetable. 

⚡️ “The FSC is not dragging its feet at all. We share the same view,” Seo said, responding to criticism over the pace of the legislation. “The direction has already been set, and while detailed discussions may be necessary in the process, there is certainly no intention on the FSC’s part to delay.”

🔗 Seo said the regulator wants the legislation passed quickly and expects discussions to proceed using bills that lawmakers have already introduced alongside the government’s proposal. Ten digital asset and stablecoin bills are currently pending in the National Assembly, giving lawmakers existing proposals to work from before the government completes its version.

69. The Miracle of Fàtima

🍀For Colin🍀

The Miracle of Fátima is the most widely recognised miracle in modern Catholicism, reportedly witnessed by almost 100,000 individuals. On October 13, 1917, a vast crowd assembled in the town of Fátima, Portugal, in response to claims made by three shepherd children, Lúcia, Francisco and Jacinta, that the Virgin Mary had appeared to them and foretold her return on that date to perform a public miracle. The event garnered substantial public and media attention, attracting devout believers but also skeptics, journalists and photographers seeking to observe and document the event.

During WW I, Portugal was gripped by hardship and despair, with widespread sentiments of war and revolution. When the shepherd children in the mountainous village of Fátima claimed to have been visited by angels, their accounts offered renewed hope to a disillusioned nation. Following the assassination of the King of Portugal and the subsequent abolition of the monarchy, the new government, dominated by Freemasons who valued science and progress over religion, implemented strict anti-clerical policies. Religious activities were suppressed, devotees arrested or exiled and the anti-Catholic laws enacted in 1911 rendered 'visions' both subversive and intolerable.

At this time, approximately 70 per cent of the peasant population in Portugal was illiterate and education was limited to agricultural labour skills. They were a simple yet devout people. Observers noted that the messages reported in the Fátima apparitions were theologically sophisticated, far beyond what uneducated children could be expected to articulate. Out of fear and skepticism, even their families doubted their claims, yet despite ridicule and hostility, the children remained steadfast in their conviction and consistent in their accounts.

During the reported miracle, numerous witnesses claimed that the silver sun appeared to dance, spin, or zigzag across the sky, plunge toward the Earth and emit radiant, multicoloured light. These phenomena allegedly lasted for about ten minutes. However, prolonged direct observation of the sun can cause solar retinopathy, leading to visual distortions such as bright colours and the illusion of movement, effects consistent with many descriptions from that day.

Some scholars have suggested the possibility of deliberate tampering with the water supply of the town, potentially inducing hallucinatory experiences among those gathered; however, not all witnesses reported observing any unusual phenomena. Photographers present at the scene captured no evidence of extraordinary occurrences, focusing instead on documenting the crowds of kneeling worshippers holding rosary beads. Given that photographic technology was already well developed and widely accessible, the absence of visual confirmation remains notable.

Is it also conceivable that the power of suggestion, intensified by the social and emotional strain of wartime, contributed to collective perception or belief? The children claimed to have witnessed visions of hell and demonic suffering so terrifying that they were overcome with fear until the Virgin Mary revealed a vision of heaven. As the sun 'rushed' toward the Earth, many in the crowd reportedly experienced similar terror. Concerned about potential government reprisal, the townspeople refrained from sharing accounts of the event until after the 1917 apparitions became widely known. Fear is the ultimate controller in the chaos of war.

Is it possible that the angelic apparitions of the late 1800s and early 1900s were manufactured by some kind of technology unknown to the people, such as the purported Project Blue Beam or a CGI effect? What kind of power would this have over Catholic countries during what was known as the Great War? Moreover, how would it affect peasant people without education? Could this event have truly been a miracle or perhaps even some kind of satanic deception? Notably, few of the prophecies eventuated. Both Fransisco and Jacinta died in a flu pandemic shortly after the apparitions.
